title: Domain Controller Performance Under LDAP Load
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Domain Controller Performance Under LDAP Load' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `operational_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `operations_domain_controller_performance_under_ldap_load` (UC-20.2.33), SOC dashboard panel "Operations — Domain Controller Performance Under LDAP Load", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:ops_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=active_directory` sourcetype='ad:dc:performance' that satisfy the UC-20.2.33 SPL filters for 'Domain Controller Performance Under LDAP Load'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.

dataSources: `index=active_directory` `sourcetype="ad:dc:performance"` Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: `Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows`, scripted performance export — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=active_directory sourcetype="ad:dc:performance" earliest=-24h
| eval ldap_ops=tonumber(coalesce(ldap_searches_sec, ldap_ops_per_sec))
| eval cpu_pct=tonumber(coalesce(cpu_utilization, cpu_load_percent))
| bin _time span=5m
| stats avg(ldap_ops) as ldap_avg avg(cpu_pct) as cpu_avg by _time, host
| eventstats median(ldap_avg) as med_ldap by host
| eval stress=if(ldap_avg>med_ldap*2.5 AND cpu_avg>80,1,0)
| where stress=1
| table _time, host, ldap_avg, cpu_avg, med_ldap

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: `Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows`, scripted performance export.
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `index=active_directory` `sourcetype="ad:dc:performance"`.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
(1) Collect NTDS `LDAP Searches/sec` and total CPU via Performance Monitor or a lightweight forwarder script into `ad:dc:performance`. (2) Tune multipliers for your baseline. (3) Escalate repeated stress windows to the identity engineering team with top calling applications from firewall or load balancer logs.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=active_directory sourcetype="ad:dc:performance" earliest=-24h
| eval ldap_ops=tonumber(coalesce(ldap_searches_sec, ldap_ops_per_sec))
| eval cpu_pct=tonumber(coalesce(cpu_utilization, cpu_load_percent))
| bin _time span=5m
| stats avg(ldap_ops) as ldap_avg avg(cpu_pct) as cpu_avg by _time, host
| eventstats median(ldap_avg) as med_ldap by host
| eval stress=if(ldap_avg>med_ldap*2.5 AND cpu_avg>80,1,0)
| where stress=1
| table _time, host, ldap_avg, cpu_avg, med_ldap
```

Understanding this SPL

**Domain Controller Performance Under LDAP Load** — Authentication and directory search storms can saturate domain controllers before generic server CPU alerts explain the blast radius. Correlating directory operation rate with CPU utilization supports extra domain controllers, load balancing changes, and misbehaving application fixes.

Documented **Data sources**: `index=active_directory` `sourcetype="ad:dc:performance"`. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): `Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows`, scripted performance export. The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: active_directory; **sourcetype**: ad:dc:performance. That sourcetype matches what this use case lists under Data sources.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=active_directory, sourcetype="ad:dc:performance", time bounds. Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **ldap_ops** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **cpu_pct** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• Discretizes time or numeric ranges with `bin`/`bucket`.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by _time, host** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• `eventstats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by host** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **stress** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• Filters the current rows with `where stress=1` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.
• Pipeline stage (see **Domain Controller Performance Under LDAP Load**): table _time, host, ldap_avg, cpu_avg, med_ldap

Enable Data Model Acceleration (and metric indexes for `mstats`) for the models or datasets referenced above; otherwise `tstats`/`mstats` may return no results from summaries.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Timeline (stress markers overlaid on CPU), Table (domain controllers with correlated spikes), Single value (stress hours per week).

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows`, scripted performance export — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=ad:dc:performance into active_directory. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`_time, cpu_avg, host, stress`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
